scope: Test/helper only; preexisting dirty source preserved; no production interfaces, global configuration, activation, architecture or new crates changed.

sourceChecks.snapshotAPI: Actual source exposes SessionManager.load_snapshot/load_native_session/snapshot_path, not store.latest_snapshot. Verification uses these real APIs after shutdown.
sourceChecks.metadataAPI: Actual source exposes SessionManager.update_meta, not update_meta_fields. Helper performs a real title/user_renamed transaction and compares stable parent identity/title/preference/working-directory/owner fields after execution.
sourceChecks.serialization: Message.tool_calls and tool_call_id bind the persisted request to its Tool result. Task results embed JSON in <route> tags.
sourceChecks.isolation: All five runtime_offline integration tests use the existing serial_test::serial(jeikcode_home) guard, including the previously unguarded mounted reload test.

persistedProof: After the completed turn and shutdown, native persisted messages equal the saved live turn exactly; non-System seeded conversation prefix remains byte-exact.
Native on-disk snapshot deserialization is lossless. Persisted assistant task arguments and matching Tool result are inspected structurally, not by whole-snapshot substring search.
Explicit persisted route asserts requested_model_id, resolved_registry_id, provider_id, resolved_api_model, effective_api_model, provider_called status and null remote identity.
Omitted persisted task arguments lack model_id; matching persisted route retains legacy_difficulty and capable-api and lacks explicit binding keys.

A second real CodingRuntime resumes the completed persisted session without submitting another UserInput. Its full non-System conversation equals the completed persisted conversation exactly, including the final task result. Shutdown and reload verify this remains persisted.
Explicit and omitted sessions are not compared byte-for-byte to one another. Only each session's own saved-turn and reopened conversation are compared.

verification.note: Default parallel test runner exercises shared guard; existing adapter boundary test uses loopback transport. No external provider network. No additional waits, retries or timeout increases were needed; no red-test run claimed. Previous task/provider/check counts not rerun or added.

conclusion: Existing native runtime/factory/session seams suffice. No new architecture or production test seam is needed. Legacy difficulty routing is proved on actual persisted native messages; legacy-owner import compatibility is not claimed.
